correctness.rationale: The source uses the correct rate law E[e^{-s lambda}]=1/(1+s^alpha). Rescaled log rate W_alpha=alpha log lambda has limiting survival 1/(1+exp(z)), derived by dominated convergence from the stated first-type Mittag-Leffler integral. An independent scipy quadrature of that integral at alpha=.20,.10,.05 and z=-.6,0,.6 converged numerically toward the logistic tail, with errors decreasing in alpha. For finitely many slow blocks the integrated jump clock divided by x_alpha^2 is exponentially tiny, and Doob maximal inequality prohibits reaching zero or moving a macroscopic fraction of x_alpha. A fast block has exponentially huge jump clock, and a half-line heat-kernel survival bound forces absorption within eta*tau_alpha. The intermediate log-rate band is negligible by logistic continuity; independent blocks then yield a geometric first-fast-block time. Weak convergence at all noninteger continuity points and bounded-transform convergence follow. No expectation convergence or uniformity in kappa is inferred.
